documents.title: History and Physical - Admission
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of evaluation: 23:40, HD1
Chief complaint: cough, fever, shortness of breath x 4 days; new confusion
HPI:
56 yo male brought to ED by son with 4 days of productive cough, subjective fevers, chills, and progressive dyspnea.
Sputum described as rust colored. Pleuritic right sided chest pain worse with deep breath.
New confusion per son, who reports patient is normally independent, works full time, drives, manages own medications.
Son states pt became vague and repetitive this afternoon and did not recognize the street where they live.
On arrival pt oriented to self only. Could not state month or place. No focal weakness or facial droop reported.
Multiple episodes of nonbloody emesis today, has not kept down fluids or food since this morning.
No chest pressure at rest, no orthopnea, no PND, no leg swelling, no hemoptysis, no diarrhea.
No recent travel, no sick contacts other than a grandchild with a cold 10 days ago. No known TB exposure.
Past medical history:
Type 2 diabetes, HTN, hyperlipidemia, former smoker (30 pack-years, quit 6 years ago), GERD.
No prior pneumonia, no asthma or COPD diagnosis, no known immunodeficiency.
Surgical history: appendectomy remote, right inguinal hernia repair.
Home medications:
metformin 1000 mg PO BID
lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
omeprazole 20 mg PO daily
aspirin 81 mg PO daily
Allergies: penicillin - reported rash as a child, no airway involvement. Tolerates cephalosporins per son.
Social: lives with wife and son nearby. Alcohol 2-3 beers weekly. No illicit drugs.
Family history: father MI at 61, mother DM2.
ROS: as per HPI, otherwise negative in a limited interview given poor historian.
Vitals at triage 21:05: T 39.2 C, HR 118, BP 96/58, respiratory rate 32, SpO2 87% on RA.
Placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93% within 10 min.
Repeat 01:05 (4 hours): T 38.4 C, HR 104, BP 108/64, respiratory rate 30, SpO2 94% on 3L NC.
Physical exam:
Gen: ill appearing, flushed, mildly diaphoretic, using accessory muscles.
Neuro: awake, oriented to self only, follows simple commands, no focal deficit, no nuchal rigidity.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no oral thrush.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, JVP flat.
Resp: crackles right base and right axilla, dullness to percussion right base, decreased breath sounds RLL. No wheeze.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no edema, cap refill 3 sec.
Skin: warm, no rash.
Labs:
WBC 18.4 with 88% neutrophils, bands 12%, Hgb 13.6, plt 212
Na 131, K 3.9, Cl 98, HCO3 20, BUN 34, Cr 1.42 (no prior baseline available), glucose 244
Lactate 3.1, procalcitonin 4.8, AST 38, ALT 30, alb 3.1
VBG pH 7.44 pCO2 31
Blood cultures x2 drawn 21:30. Sputum Gram stain and culture sent. Resp viral panel and urine pneumococcal antigen sent.
Imaging:
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
Assessment/Plan:
56 yo male with severe community-acquired pneumonia, RML/RLL, with hypoxemic respiratory failure, AKI, hyponatremia, and acute encephalopathy.
CURB-65 of 3 (confusion, BUN > 19 mg/dL, respiratory rate >= 30). Admit to stepdown for close monitoring.
1. CAP: ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin 500 mg IV daily. Penicillin allergy is low risk rash, cephalosporin acceptable.
2. Hypoxemia: continue 3L NC, titrate for SpO2 >= 92%. Incentive spirometry q1h while awake.
3. Emesis/NPO: unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting, all meds IV. Ondansetron 4 mg IV q6h prn.
4. Volume/AKI: NS 1L bolus then 100 mL/hr. Hold lisinopril and metformin. Trend Cr and lactate q6h.
5. Encephalopathy: likely infectious/hypoxemic. Recheck orientation q4h. No LP at present given no meningismus.
6. Glucose: SSI moderate scale q6h while off metformin.
7. Effusion small, no thoracentesis now; repeat imaging if worsening or persistent fever.
8. Discussed with son at bedside. DVT ppx heparin 5000 units SC q8h. Full code.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:20
Subjective:
Pt slept in intervals, coughing productive of rust colored sputum. Two episodes of emesis overnight (01:30, 04:50).
Still unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting; declined breakfast, sipped water and vomited.
Now oriented to self and son's name, not to place or month. Son reports confusion improved from admission.
Vitals overnight/this AM:
T max 38.7 at 03:00, T 37.9 now. HR 96-112, BP 112/66, respiratory rate 26, SpO2 92% on 3L NC.
Still on 3L NC. Did not tolerate weaning trial to 2L at 05:00, desat to 89%.
Urine output 720 mL over 12 h.
Exam:
Gen: less diaphoretic, appears fatigued.
Resp: crackles right base and right mid lung, dullness right base unchanged, no wheeze, mild accessory muscle use.
CV: tachycardic regular, no murmur.
Abd: soft, nontender. Ext: no edema.
Neuro: intermittently inattentive, no focal deficit.
Labs 05:30:
WBC 15.8, Hgb 13.1, plt 205, Na 133, K 4.0, HCO3 21, BUN 30, Cr 1.24, glucose 188, lactate 1.8
Blood cultures x2 no growth at 12 h. Sputum culture pending, Gram stain gram positive diplococci. Resp viral panel negative.
Assessment/Plan:
Severe CAP, RML/RLL with small right pleural effusion, improving clinically but still O2 and antiemetic dependent.
1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin. Day 2 of therapy.
2. O2: keep 3L NC, retry wean this afternoon. Incentive spirometry, ambulate with RN.
3. Emesis: switch ondansetron to scheduled 4 mg IV q8h, add IV fluids 75 mL/hr. All meds remain IV.
4. AKI improving, Cr 1.42 -> 1.24. Continue holding lisinopril and metformin.
5. Follow up urine pneumococcal antigen and sputum culture; narrow abx when speciated.
6. Delirium precautions, orient q shift, minimize nighttime interruptions.
7. Repeat CXR if fever persists > 48 h or oxygen requirement climbs.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 16:10 (interval/afternoon)
Subjective:
Seen at bedside with son present. Pt more interactive, now oriented to self, son, and hospital; still unsure of month.
Tried clear liquids at 13:00 and vomited once at 13:40. Remains unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting.
Cough less painful, sputum now yellow rather than rust colored.
Vitals 15:45: T 37.4, HR 92, BP 118/70, respiratory rate 22, SpO2 94% on 3L NC.
Wean trial at 14:30 to 2L: SpO2 dropped to 90% with ambulation, returned to 3L NC.
Exam:
Resp: crackles right base, right mid lung crackles softer than AM, no accessory muscle use at rest.
CV: regular rate, no murmur. Abd soft. No edema.
Neuro: attentive through most of interview, follows 3-step command.
Results this afternoon:
Urine pneumococcal antigen positive. Sputum culture prelim S. pneumoniae, sensitivities pending.
Blood cultures x2 no growth at 20 h.
Assessment/Plan:
Severe CAP, pneumococcal, RML/RLL infiltrate with small right pleural effusion. Clinically improving on HD2.
1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin pending sensitivities; plan step down to oral once emesis resolves.
2. O2 3L NC maintained; repeat wean in AM with ambulation oximetry.
3. Emesis: continue scheduled ondansetron IV, add metoclopramide 5 mg IV prn x1. Advance to clears at 20:00 if no emesis.
4. IVF continue 75 mL/hr, recheck BMP in AM.
5. SSI q6h, CBG 162 at 16:00.
6. Effusion small and stable by exam, no drainage indicated.
7. PT eval ordered. Anticipate discharge HD3 if tolerating oral intake and off O2 or stable on room air.
8. Updated son on plan, questions answered.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD3
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Length of stay: 3 days, discharged HD3 at 15:20
Discharge diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, right middle and right lower lobe, pneumococcal, with small right pleural effusion
Secondary: acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (resolved), acute encephalopathy (resolved), AKI (resolved), hyponatremia (resolved), T2DM, HTN, HLD
Hospital course:
56 yo male presented with 4 days of cough, fever, dyspnea and new confusion per son, who reports patient is normally independent. Oriented to self only on arrival.
At triage respiratory rate 32 and SpO2 87% on RA; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%. Respiratory rate 30 at 4 hours.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note; admitted to stepdown.
Started on ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin. Blood cultures x2 remained negative; urine pneumococcal antigen positive and sputum culture grew pan-sensitive S. pneumoniae.
Unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, managed with IV fluids and scheduled IV ondansetron; all meds given IV.
Still on 3L NC on hospital day 2 with failed wean attempts at 05:00 and 14:30.
HD3: tolerated full liquids and then soft diet without emesis, weaned to room air by 10:00 with SpO2 95% at rest and 93% after ambulating 200 feet.
Mental status returned to baseline HD3, oriented x4, son confirms back to normal self.
Cr 1.42 on admission improved to 1.02. Na 131 -> 138. WBC 18.4 -> 10.2. Afebrile > 24 h at discharge.
Discharge vitals 14:30: T 36.9, HR 82, BP 124/76, RR 18, SpO2 95% RA.
Discharge exam: comfortable, mild crackles right base, no accessory muscle use, abdomen soft, no edema, oriented x4.
Discharge medications:
amoxicillin 1 g PO TID x 4 more days (to complete 7 day course; penicillin allergy label reviewed, childhood rash, tolerated ceftriaxone inpatient)
guaifenesin 200 mg PO q4h prn cough
ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h prn nausea, #12
resume metformin 1000 mg PO BID
resume lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
resume atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily, omeprazole 20 mg PO daily, aspirin 81 mg PO daily
Follow up:
Primary care in 5-7 days for clinical recheck and BMP.
Repeat chest imaging in 6-8 weeks given smoking history and effusion.
Instructions:
Finish all antibiotic doses. Use incentive spirometer 10x per hour while awake. Walk several times daily. Drink fluids.
Return for fever > 38.3, worsening shortness of breath, confusion, chest pain, or inability to keep down fluids.
Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination discussed, to be given at primary care once recovered.
Discharge condition: stable, ambulating on room air, tolerating diet. Discharged home with wife and son.
Pending at discharge: none. Final sputum sensitivities reviewed prior to discharge.
